events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to St. Joseph first.** My pier rating is about **3 of 4 (good)**.
- **South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon** each look like about **2 of 4 (average)**. Grand Haven and Muskegon are roughly tied, and South Haven is a little behind them.
- **Lures:** start with spoons, and add rotators or flies at St. Joseph.
- **Depth:** fish near the surface and shallow mid-water first. Adjust once you find fish.
- **Check the pier before you go.** No pier reports exist for these weeks, so these ratings are estimates from boat reports.

## Why
- **St. Joseph ranks first:** the newest report there rated boat salmon fishing good (3), and the bite was spoons, rotators and flies (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).
- **The other three rank lower:** their newest boat reports were average (2) or not rated, and the Muskegon and South Haven reports were weaker a week earlier (Muskegon, 2023-07-19; South Haven, 2023-07-19).
- **Shallow fish matter for a pier:** St. Joseph reported some fish at 30 and 50 feet (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26), which is closer to pier range than the deep water most boats fished.
- **I'd expect pier results to follow nearby boat results,** since I found no pier-specific data for this period.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest 2023-07-26, six days old; all salmon reports were from boats)
- St. Joseph (2023-07-26): quality 3, "Salmon anglers continued to have good success." Fish were most consistent around 120 feet, with some caught at 30 and 50 feet. Spoons caught most fish; rotators and flies also caught fish.
- South Haven (2023-07-26): quality 2, "decent fishing." Best water was around 110 feet; rotators, flies and meat rigs worked best.
- Grand Haven (2023-07-26): not rated. Fish were 60-120 feet down in 80-140 feet of water, on orange or green spoons and yellow or green meat rigs.
- Muskegon (2023-07-26): quality 2, "fair." Fish were 60-100 feet down in 90-150 feet of water, on green or glow spoons and green meat rigs.
- Earlier in July, Muskegon and South Haven were rated 1 (below average) on 2023-07-19 and 2023-07-05.

**Past seasons** (history, not current)
- In similar water temperatures (about 74 F) in late July and early August, past boat reports ranged from slow (0) to good (3). Those reports were mostly from boats, and the best results often came in low light (Grand Haven, 2022-08-03; Muskegon, 2022-08-03; St. Joseph, 2022-08-03).
- South Haven's piers were closed to fishing for several days in August 2022 because of red flag lake conditions (South Haven, 2022-08-10). Check for closures before you go.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water in the most recent week averaged 75 F at St. Joseph, 74 F at South Haven, and 72 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon. Those readings are measured, but they are for the last week of July (current conditions tool, backtest mode).
- The tool did not return a modeled pierhead temperature, a cold-layer depth, or a wind forecast. I can't tell whether an upwelling is happening.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): mature Chinook in early fall tend to hold in water near 55 F or colder. Surface water at 72-75 F is well above that, so the fish are probably deeper than the pier's surface water.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old and covers the week of July 24-26. Conditions may have changed since then.
- None of these reports covers pier fishing, so the pier ratings are my estimates from boat reports.
- The conditions data was from backtest mode. It had no pierhead temperature, cold-layer depth or wind forecast, so I can't say whether conditions are improving or declining.
- Holland was not included in this search. Grand Haven and South Haven are the nearest reporting ports.

## Sources
- St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon, DNR bulletin for 2023-07-26: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3675eed
- DNR bulletin for 2023-07-19: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
- DNR bulletin for 2022-08-10 (South Haven pier closure): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/327890a
- DNR bulletin for 2022-08-03 (historical comparison): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
